---
title: "Overview"
---

Code for the analysis of vapour pressure deficit (VPD) and soil water content (SWC)
effects on daytime net ecosystem productivity (NEP) at forest eddy covariance sites.

One XGBoost model is trained per site. The fitted models are then interpreted with
SHAP values (per-sample contributions, calculated out-of-sample through 5-fold
cross-validation) and with ALE curves (isolated feature effects). Site-level results
are aggregated with equal weight per site, both overall and by IGBP forest type.

- Target: `NEP_ZSCORE`, half-hourly, daytime, four months of highest GPP per site.
  `GPP_ZSCORE`, `RECO_ZSCORE` and `ET_ZSCORE` run through the same pipeline as
  supporting analyses
- Features: `TA_ZSCORE`, `SWIN_ZSCORE`, `VPD_ZSCORE`, `SWC_ZSCORE`
- All variables are z-scored within site, so sites with different absolute ranges
  can be compared

## What is in the repository

| Path | Contents |
|------|----------|
| `scripts/10_datasets/` | Find and merge source datasets, check variable coverage, add ERA5 climate normals |
| `scripts/20_subsets/` | Build the per-site analysis subset and calculate z-scores |
| `scripts/30_shap/` | Train XGBoost models, calculate SHAP values and ALE curves |
| `scripts/40_aggregation/` | Aggregate SHAP values per site, across sites, by IGBP, by stress stage |
| `scripts/50_figures/` | Manuscript figures and tables |
| `src/` | Shared code: models, aggregation, plotting, statistics, file handling, paths |
| `config/` | `settings.yaml` and FLUXNET site metadata |
| `data/worldmap/` | Natural Earth country outlines used by the map figure |

Source data and analysis outputs are **not** in the repository. See [Data](data.qmd).

## Where to start

Start with [Installation](installation.qmd), then point the code at a data folder as
described in [Data](data.qmd). [Pipeline](pipeline.qmd) lists the scripts in the order
they run and what each one writes. [Figures](figures.qmd) maps manuscript figures to
the scripts that produce them.
